Internal helper: lay out a printed call that is wider than the message

Source: R/utils.R
dot-jst_layout_call.Rd

Ruling R5 (Jeff, Session 345; built Session 353): every call the package prints for pasting has ONE layout.

  1. Within the message width, one line.

  2. Wider, broken where R allows: after a comma between the call's arguments, each later line at a FIXED indent four spaces in from the call's own – not hung under the opening parenthesis, which a long name pushes far right. As many arguments go on a line as fit. An argument that will not fit on a line of its own breaks inside (.jst_break_arg()): a map or labels string after its semicolons, its rules set under the first, and a c(...) after its commas.

  3. Never left as one long line, never shortened with "...", never broken by the prose wrapper: it runs as printed.

A map broken over lines still runs: the map parsers trim each rule, so the line break and the spaces after it are dropped with the space a one-line map has there.

Usage

.jst_layout_call(line, width)

Arguments

line

Character(1): one indented line holding one call, or an assignment whose right side is a call or a subscript (the mydata <- d[rows, cols] a message offers for an expression given as the data, broken after the commas inside its brackets).

width

The message width for the line.

Value

Character(1), with newlines where it was broken.

Details

Called from .jst_wrap_message(), so it holds for every emitter and every function; until Session 353 .jst_jencode_map_call() packed its own maps, hung under the parenthesis at a fixed 76 columns, and every other call ran on past the width. A line it cannot read as one call – two calls, a comment, a call with text after it – is returned unchanged.
